Using the identities:

\[
2\cos^2\frac{\theta}{2}=1+\cos\theta
\]

and

\[
\sin\left(\theta+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=\frac{\sqrt2}{2}(\sin\theta+\cos\theta),
\]

the expression becomes

\[
\frac{1+\cos\theta-\sin\theta-1}{\sqrt2\cdot \frac{\sqrt2}{2}(\sin\theta+\cos\theta)}
=
\frac{\cos\theta-\sin\theta}{\sin\theta+\cos\theta}.
\]

Divide numerator and denominator by \(\cos\theta\):

\[
\frac{1-\tan\theta}{\tan\theta+1}.
\]

Given \(\tan\theta=-2\sqrt2\),

\[
\frac{1-(-2\sqrt2)}{-2\sqrt2+1}
=
\frac{1+2\sqrt2}{1-2\sqrt2}
=
-\frac{9+4\sqrt2}{7}.
\]

\[
\boxed{-\frac{9+4\sqrt2}{7}}
\]
